description: Gives your AI assistant your career history: it saves and scores job postings, tailors a resume to each one from things you actually did, renders the PDF, and tracks your applications. Needs Maestro Career Studio running on your computer: uv tool install --python 3.12 maestro-career-studio, then maestro start. 88 tools; your data stays on your machine.

profile.title: Tool profile
profile.description: full (88 tools) or a scoped set: hunt, apply, explore, templates, career. Enable one at a time — the scoped profiles are subsets of full, so more than one costs context without adding capability.

backend_url.title: Maestro address
backend_url.description: Where Maestro Career Studio is running. Change it only if you moved the backend port.

tool_signatures.name: get_job_search_brief
tool_signatures.description: your profile, constraints, resume summaries, sync status (enabled, role) and an applying block (answer_level: your Screening answers setting, facts, history or queued); call first in a job-search chat. It holds your work-permit answers for each country you apply in (work_auth_by_country; the one home set, work_auth, stays for one release), when each automation last finished a run that didn't fail (last_runs, where the job hunt and mail status start, an hour earlier), and the role list (roles).

tool_signatures.name: sync_now
tool_signatures.description: ask the always-on copy to sync now; returns the round's outcome and per-step counts. On your laptop, it explains that your bot runs the sync; with sync off, it says "Sync isn't set up."

tool_signatures.name: find_job_by_url
tool_signatures.description: check whether a posting is already saved.

tool_signatures.name: store_extracted_jd
tool_signatures.description: save a job. Your assistant fills in the job's details in the format the tool describes. Saving scores the job against every base resume you can pick for it. apply_url records the application address when it differs from the posting's. Saving a job that's already saved returns it unchanged, unless update=true: then the new details correct it in place (same job, status and applications), the reply's correction says what changed, and when something scoring reads changed the job's match scores are replaced with fresh ones. A correction can't be undone.

tool_signatures.name: list_jobs, get_job
tool_signatures.description: saved jobs (a short paginated list, then one job in full), with ownership to identify jobs owned here and replicas. Each job carries its stage: saved, scored, gaps, tailored, pdf_ready, applied or closed.

tool_signatures.name: list_referrals, save_referral
tool_signatures.description: referral contacts; save_referral adds one (company and careers page) or, given its referral_id, changes only the fields you pass (also in apply and track).

tool_signatures.name: list_applications, get_application
tool_signatures.description: your applications (a short paginated list, then one in full).

tool_signatures.name: update_application
tool_signatures.description: set status, applied date, notes or referral; clear=["notes"] or ["referral_id"] empties them.

tool_signatures.name: export_jobs
tool_signatures.description: export filtered job rows for analysis.

tool_signatures.name: list_base_resumes, get_base_resume
tool_signatures.description: your base resumes; include_archived=true lists the archived ones too.

tool_signatures.name: edit_base_resume
tool_signatures.description: change parts of a base resume and re-render its PDF. The tool's own description lists the edit types.

tool_signatures.name: update_base_resume, create_base_resume
tool_signatures.description: replace or create a whole base resume.

tool_signatures.name: duplicate_base_resume, archive_base_resume, unarchive_base_resume
tool_signatures.description: copy, hide or restore one (archiving deletes nothing).

tool_signatures.name: set_base_resume_identity
tool_signatures.description: set what a resume is for — its countries, role, company and focus. A resume set for some countries is scored and recommended only for jobs in them.

tool_signatures.name: list_resume_versions, get_resume_version, restore_resume_version
tool_signatures.description: every saved version of a resume; restoring adds a new version and deletes nothing.

tool_signatures.name: run_health_check, get_health_report
tool_signatures.description: score a resume on its own, without a job, and list what to fix.

tool_signatures.name: judge_health_bullets
tool_signatures.description: store your assistant's judgment of each bullet, by the app's own rubric, so the check can grade. It is used when Maestro's own AI doesn't judge: with no model key in the app, or when your assistant writes (see [Who writes](#who-writes)), even with a key.

tool_signatures.name: waive_health_gate, unwaive_health_gate
tool_signatures.description: skip a failing check only when you say so, or undo that.

tool_signatures.name: score_ats
tool_signatures.description: score one resume, or all your base resumes set for the job's country, against a job.

tool_signatures.name: compare_ats
tool_signatures.description: before/after scores for a tailored application.

tool_signatures.name: create_tailoring_session, list_tailoring_sessions, get_tailoring_session, close_tailoring_session
tool_signatures.description: start, find, resume or abandon a gap walkthrough. These are the same sessions as the web app's gap page, so you can start in one and finish in the other. With use_presets=true, create_tailoring_session also fills the gaps from your saved Quick tailor presets instead of walking them one by one.

tool_signatures.name: resolve_gaps
tool_signatures.description: save your answer for each gap (add a keyword, describe real experience, attach a project, skip, or "can't confirm" so it's never asked again).

tool_signatures.name: tailor_session
tool_signatures.description: turn your answers into a tailored application, make its PDF and show the before/after score. Your assistant passes its own edits (ops), or no_new_text=true to apply only the answers that need no new wording (a hidden entry, an approved career-history bullet, saved keywords into Skills), with no AI at all; Maestro's AI writes the edits only when you chose it (see [Who writes](#who-writes)). Edits your assistant writes itself must read in first person ("Built X"); a third-person line is refused with an error naming it. The reply names unbacked_skills, skills it put on your resume that your career history doesn't back, and answers_left_to_ops, answers still waiting for wording.

tool_signatures.name: edit_application
tool_signatures.description: make a further fix to a tailored application, keeping earlier edits.

tool_signatures.name: render_pdf
tool_signatures.description: render a base resume or an application. A template_id alone is a one-off; with keep=true the template and look settings (formatting) are saved on that resume first, so later renders and edits keep them. Only a ready template is kept.

tool_signatures.name: get_rendered_pdf
tool_signatures.description: save the PDF locally with one PNG per page, and report any em dashes.

tool_signatures.name: get_rendered_pdf_page_image
tool_signatures.description: fetch one page image, for clients that can't open local files.

tool_signatures.name: prepare_application_pdf_upload
tool_signatures.description: save a copy of the application PDF where the browser tool can upload it; document="cover_letter" stages the stored cover letter's PDF beside it (made first when needed; refused when no letter is stored). It does not submit anything.

tool_signatures.name: get_autofill_profile
tool_signatures.description: your stored form-fill details (contact, work authorization, consented EEO answers).

tool_signatures.name: generate_qa_answers
tool_signatures.description: Maestro's AI writes answers to an application's screening questions, only when you chose Maestro's AI to write (see [Who writes](#who-writes)).

tool_signatures.name: generate_cover_letter
tool_signatures.description: Maestro's AI writes a cover letter in the tone you ask for, under the same setting.

tool_signatures.name: store_qa_answers, store_cover_letter
tool_signatures.description: keep answers or a cover letter your assistant wrote itself, with no AI key in Maestro. The letter replaces the saved one and gets its PDF; both show on the job's Apply step.

tool_signatures.name: list_qa_entries
tool_signatures.description: the answers and cover letters saved so far.

tool_signatures.name: set_autofill_profile
tool_signatures.description: save the form answers you give: contact and address, work permits for each country you apply in, start and pay, education, languages and your own questions. Only what it is given changes, merged into your saved answers at the moment it saves, so an answer the Companion learned meanwhile stays. Your own questions are added or updated by question, never removed (removing one is yours, in Profile).

tool_signatures.name: set_markets
tool_signatures.description: where you live, where you apply, and the currency pay reads in, as one save: if one part is refused, nothing changes.

tool_signatures.name: set_job_preferences
tool_signatures.description: the roles, places, work mode and lowest pay you want. A role the list doesn't know is refused with the closest ones it has.

tool_signatures.name: set_persona
tool_signatures.description: a few sentences on your direction and strengths, in your words; writing prompts read it for tone.

tool_signatures.name: propose_application, list_proposals, get_proposal
tool_signatures.description: file a job your assistant found for your review, and read the queue.

tool_signatures.name: record_triage
tool_signatures.description: accept or decline proposals; accepted ones are queued for the next apply run.

tool_signatures.name: request_decision, record_decision, resume_proposal, report_failure
tool_signatures.description: handle proposals that need your input or hit a problem.

tool_signatures.name: get_final_review
tool_signatures.description: everything to check before you approve, including the flagged answers.

tool_signatures.name: record_filled_answers
tool_signatures.description: records what was filled on each form page and where each answer came from; its flags show again in get_final_review.

tool_signatures.name: record_consent
tool_signatures.description: record your approve/reject after you answer, or the agent's automatic approval with channel auto while full automation is On. Auto approval requires a Queued proposal, final-review evidence, a company off the skip list and a daily-cap slot.

tool_signatures.name: get_job_site_login
tool_signatures.description: the saved job-site email and password, only while full automation is On, for a Queued or approved proposal off the skip list. Each hand-off is audited without the value; the login passes through your agent's AI provider. Use it only for job-site accounts.

tool_signatures.name: record_run
tool_signatures.description: record one finished automation run; it appears under Recent runs on the Automations page.

tool_signatures.name: attach_evidence
tool_signatures.description: attach the final-review screenshot and, when using receipt evidence, the submission confirmation, either as the image itself or as the path of a screenshot saved on this computer (PNG or JPEG, up to 5 MB), so its bytes never pass through the chat.

tool_signatures.name: mark_submitted
tool_signatures.description: mark an approved proposal as submitted with receipt evidence or the user's attestation. While full automation is On, channel auto records the agent's word with a note naming what confirmed submission (at least one letter or digit); a receipt is optional. It can also confirm submission_uncertain, without another submit click.

tool_signatures.name: get_career_context
tool_signatures.description: your full career record, as structured data or, with format="markdown", as career.md.

tool_signatures.name: kb_list_entities, kb_get_entity, kb_list_points
tool_signatures.description: browse entries and points, with their IDs.

tool_signatures.name: kb_capture, kb_add_points, kb_ingest_resume, kb_sync_base
tool_signatures.description: add new material as draft points for you to approve. kb_add_points takes bullets your assistant already wrote for an entry, with no AI call; kb_capture has Maestro's AI write them, only when you chose it (see [Who writes](#who-writes)). kb_sync_base keeps a rephrased bullet as a wording of the one it rewrites instead of a new draft.

tool_signatures.name: kb_edit_point, kb_create_entity, kb_edit_entity, kb_edit_profile
tool_signatures.description: correct or add entries.

tool_signatures.name: kb_approve_points
tool_signatures.description: mark draft points approved, only after you have approved them. It never retires; that is kb_retire_points.

tool_signatures.name: kb_groom_entity
tool_signatures.description: find similar bullets on one entry, grouped, with one proposed to keep. Reads only, no AI call.

tool_signatures.name: kb_combine_points, kb_retire_points
tool_signatures.description: fold similar points into the one you keep, or stop using a stale one, only after you said yes. Resumes keep their text, and /career undoes both.

tool_signatures.name: kb_merge_entities
tool_signatures.description: fold a duplicate entry (one an import split off) into the one you keep, only after you said yes: its bullets, documents and resume links move over and the duplicate goes. A merge can't be undone.

tool_signatures.name: create_base_resume_from_kb
tool_signatures.description: build a new base resume from approved entries.

tool_signatures.name: list_templates, get_template
tool_signatures.description: resume templates (LaTeX or Typst).

tool_signatures.name: create_template_draft, update_template_draft, validate_template
tool_signatures.description: create, edit and test-compile a template.

tool_signatures.name: explore_trends
tool_signatures.description: one chart's rows per call, by view: top_skills and heatmap (which skills your saved jobs ask for), role_mix (roles per week), fit_distribution (how each base resume's match scores spread), ats_over_time (match score per week) and tailoring_lift (how much tailoring helps). Every view but fit_distribution takes the role, level and employment-type filters; top_skills and heatmap take a limit.

tool_signatures.name: explore_gap_frequency
tool_signatures.description: which skills keep showing up as gaps across your saved jobs.
